translated_text: Paris, April 30, 1940. My darling! And my sweetheart, no letter from you this morning—maybe this evening… Last night I had a long conversation with Mother. She promised to be nicer and not get angry so often—we'll see. The paper went out yesterday. But they don't have issue #5. They'll send it when they have it. But for now, next week, when they have it, you'll have #2, 3, and 4. Tomorrow I'm going to see a good Hungarian doctor who was recommended to me. I'll start treatment with him. It's going well, but before this specialist's treatment, I want to get a second opinion. And you, my little one, have you bought the shoes? How free am I to buy them? If Sperr or Bichal don't call me today, I'll call them tomorrow. They're a nuisance!… My darling, I kiss you a thousand times with all my affection and hold you so tight in my arms. Your Baba is doing much better! (Fi TENTE AANCE) NA PARIS RUE 8 50 46945 APRIL DES 40 FUCINES TENTEZ NATI Mr. Robert Zweigenthal chez R. 1.
